title: Azure Monitor -- metrics, Log Analytics, KQL basics
exp: Azure Monitor is the direct equivalent of CloudWatch -- the platform-native observability service everything else, including Grafana, ultimately reads from.
pts: Azure Monitor Metrics: near-real-time numeric time-series data, collected automatically for most resources with no setup required.
Log Analytics workspace: a centralized store for logs, queried with KQL (Kusto Query Language) -- similar to a CloudWatch Logs group but typically shared tenant-wide.

Diagnostic settings route a resource's logs/metrics INTO a Log Analytics workspace -- this routing is NOT automatic and must be explicitly configured per resource, the most common 'why is there no data' issue for people new to Azure Monitor.
KQL basics: TableName | where condition | summarize aggregation by field | order by field -- structurally close to Logs Insights' fields/filter/stats/sort pattern, different keyword names.
bin() groups timestamps into time buckets -- the one KQL function that transfers with zero translation from Logs Insights, literally the same name and behavior.
Metric Alerts fire on Metrics thresholds; Log Alerts fire on a KQL query's result count -- two alert types under the same Azure Monitor Alerts umbrella.
code:
az monitor log-analytics workspace create \
  --resource-group rg-orders-pipeline --workspace-name law-orders-pipeline

az monitor diagnostic-settings create \
  --name "databricks-to-law" \
  --resource "/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-orders-pipeline/providers/Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces/dbx-orders-pipeline" \
  --workspace "law-orders-pipeline" \
  --logs '[{"category":"clusters","enabled":true},{"category":"jobs","enabled":true}]'

// KQL -- find recent errors
PipelineLogs_CL
| where Level_s == "ERROR"
| project TimeGenerated, Source_s, Message_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| limit 50

// Aggregate by source, time-bucketed
PipelineLogs_CL
| where Source_s == "Bloomberg"
| summarize AvgDuration = avg(DurationMs_d) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)

qa.q: Why do people often see 'no data' in Log Analytics right after creating a resource?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Unlike CloudWatch where many AWS services log automatically to a default location, Azure resources don't send logs into a Log Analytics workspace automatically -- a Diagnostic Setting must be explicitly created, specifying which log categories to route and to which workspace. This one-time configuration step is the single most common source of confusion for people new to Azure Monitor.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

qa.q: What is the one KQL function that transfers with zero translation from CloudWatch Logs Insights?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** bin() -- used for grouping timestamps into time buckets, named identically and behaving the same way in both languages. The rest of the syntax differs in keyword (where vs filter, summarize vs stats, project vs fields) but expresses the same pipe-based query structure.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** T-SQL engine parses, compiles into execution plans, caches them in the plan cache, and executes via the storage engine (buffer pool & latching).

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Parameter sniffing and missing stats cause sub-optimal plan compilation, resulting in full table scans and high CPU.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Parameterization improves plan reuse, but recompile hints (OPTION RECOMPILE) may be needed for skewed data distributions.
